To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

pyrolysis is not a suitable treatment and disposal option for chrome tanned LFT and CS from tanneries as it results in the formation of a high concentration of hazardous gaseous emission, which is a major concern.
pyrolysis can be a potential treatment option for chrome tanned solid wastes from tanning industry, which can produce bio-oil, char and gas, which can be utilized as a fuel for power generation.
the pyrolysis of chrome tanned leather wastes is a potential alternative for incineration, which can be used to recover energy from the leather wastes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the investigation on pyrolytic and incineration processes for the treatment and disposal of chrome tanned leather wastes from tannery.
the investigation of thermal treatment of chrome tanned leather waste from tannery industry for effective treatment and safe disposal.

a detailed investigation on the pyrolysis of leather trimmings and chrome shavings from tanneries and incineration for effective treatment and safe disposal, which could pave a way for circular economy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

incineration of leather solid wastes from chrome tanned tanneries could be a potential option for the effective disposal of the solid waste and the residual ash obtained from incineration could also be utilized in the metallurgical industry.
pyrolysis of chrome tanned leather trimmings could be a potential alternative to incineration for the treatment and disposal of the chrome tanned leather waste from tannery industry.

incineration is an efficient method to treat and dispose of chrome tanned leather waste from tannery, which can be used as a potential source of energy, and the residual ash can be used as raw material for the production of chemicals and ferrochrome alloy, which would help to reduce the environmental impact of the tannery industry.

incineration can be a better option for the disposal and treatment of leather solid waste in developing countries.

pyrolysis of chrome tanned leather trimmings and shavings is a viable option for the production of bio oil with potential utilization in the energy and chemical industries and incineration could provide a potential solution for treatment and disposal of chrome tanned shavings and trimmings.
incineration is a better treatment and disposal option for chrome tanned solid wastes from tanning industry.
